class: Development only. No training; no change to VisionJob, summarise_track, search semantics, plate-control contracts, release profiles or the frozen P3 evidence. O3 stays open.

cpuTiming.execution: a fixed pool of 10 worker processes, each one ORT session with 1 intra-op and 1 inter-op thread; the machine, worker count and thread settings are recorded
cpuTiming.passes: three timed full OCR passes on one machine with ORT threads fixed at 1: phase 1 (read), phase 2 (repeat) and phase 2T (a third timing pass whose readings must also be canonical-equal to phase 1)
cpuTiming.perPassStatistic: process CPU time of each FastPlateOcrRecogniser.read call (RGB conversion, resize, ORT run, decode), summed per track; S1 uses lr-005's call only; image decode CPU recorded separately
cpuTiming.reported: median over the three passes of the mean per-track CPU ms, per policy cost class; aggregation CPU measured by timing the policy computation over all tracks three times (median), reported as measured

data.partition: LRLPR-26 train only (20,000 tracks); held test archives are unlabelled and unused
data.recognitionInputs: lr-001..lr-005 only, in frame order; HR frames and corners are never recognition inputs
data.truth: normalise(plate_text) with mavi-plate-normalisation-v1; no format-based correction

decision.scope: informs the O3 aggregation question only; changes no Production behaviour and decides no architecture

step1.applies: each selected, feasible family X in {C*, A*}
supportedAgainstU: upper bound of the 95% CI of (incorrectTextAcceptance(X) - incorrectTextAcceptance(U)) < 0
point estimate of recall loss (recall(U) - recall(X)) <= 0.030
upper bound of the 95% CI of the recall loss <= 0.050

step2.bothSupported: A* preferred only if the paired A* - C* CI favours A* and excludes 0 on at least one of correctTextRecall, incorrectTextAcceptance, coverage, and no measure (the five directional measures) has a CI that favours C* and excludes 0; otherwise C* (simplicity default, not an equivalence claim). Higher OCR confidence alone is never a reason to prefer A*
step2.favours: for a 'higher' measure, a CI with lower bound > 0 favours the minuend and upper bound < 0 the subtrahend; for a 'lower' measure the reverse

step3.INCONCLUSIVE: any other valid run (indeterminate evidence, not a negative result)
step3.NOT SUPPORTED: every family (C and A) has negative evidence: (a) INFEASIBLE on DEV, or (b) lower bound of the CI of (incorrectTextAcceptance(X) - incorrectTextAcceptance(U)) >= 0, or (c) lower bound of the CI of the recall loss > 0.030
step3.SUPPORTED: at least one family is SUPPORTED in step 1; report the step-2 preferred policy and its configuration

eligibleWhen: the OCR call returned exactly one reading whose raw text satisfies contracts.is_raw_text and whose confidence is a finite probability in [0, 1]

ineligibleCauses.empty: the adapter returned no reading (empty text)
ineligibleCauses.ocrError: the image could not be decoded or the OCR call raised (including the adapter's non-finite-confidence refusal)
ineligibleCauses.outputInvalid: more than one reading, a raw text failing is_raw_text, or a confidence that is not a finite probability (pipeline.py abstains such a crop)

eligibility.ineligibleFrame: contributes no text, no support and no weight; still counts in the OCR-call cost
eligibility.n: number of eligible readings of the track, 0..5
eligibility.support: s(t) = number of eligible readings whose normalised text is t
eligibility.weight: w(t) = exact sum (fractions.Fraction of each float64 confidence) of the confidences of those readings

INVALID: an inventory, manifest or archive hash mismatch
a phase-2 (or phase-2T) repeat that is not canonical-equal to phase 1
a missing or mismatched selection.json SHA, or a parameter-file SHA mismatch
a split-file SHA mismatch (or a rules-file SHA mismatch)
integrity.consequence: execution stops; no scientific outcome; no partial metrics reported as results; the run may be repeated only after the defect is fixed, with no change to these rules

measures.correctTextRecall: tracks whose truth is among the accepted texts / tracks
measures.cost: OCR calls per track (1 for S1, 5 otherwise) and CPU ms per track
measures.coverage: tracks with at least one accepted text / tracks
measures.denominator: all tracks of the scored population; abstentions stay in the denominator and are neither correct nor incorrect
measures.incorrectTextAcceptance: tracks accepting at least one text other than the truth / tracks
measures.predictionPrecision: correct accepted (track, text) pairs / accepted pairs; undefined (null) when there are no accepted pairs
measures.unionConvention: a U track accepting a correct and an incorrect text counts towards both recall and incorrect-text acceptance
measures.wrongTextsPerTrack: accepted non-truth texts / tracks, with the distribution of tracks by 0, 1, >=2 wrong texts

ocr.call: FastPlateOcrRecogniser.read(region=the whole LR image opened with Pillow, verified=None, box=None); the adapter converts to RGB and resizes internally; plate detection is bypassed (each LR image is already a plate crop)
ocr.rank0: the adapter emits at most one reading; that reading is rank 0

parameters.floorComparison: confidence >= ocrConfidenceFloor (inclusive), the pipeline.py PLATE_READ rule

policies.A: t* = text with the largest w; accept t* iff s(t*) >= 2, no other text has equal w (exact), Sigma w over all eligible readings is finite and > 0 (else abstain: zero-weight guard), and w(t*)/Sigma w >= tau, evaluated exactly with fractions (tau as the exact decimal); else abstain
policies.C: t* = text with the largest support; accept t* iff s(t*) >= k and no other text has equal support; else abstain
policies.S1: accept the reading of lr-005 if eligible, else abstain; never consults other frames; OCR calls per track: 1
policies.SB: accept the eligible reading with the highest confidence; a tie goes to the lowest frame index; abstain if n=0
policies.U: accept every distinct eligible normalised text (MAVI's current union: floor + summarise_track's distinct rank-0 normalised texts); empty (abstain) if n=0
policies.U-raw: SECONDARY, excluded from the decision: union of every ok-normalised rank-0 text with no floor (frames with empty, ocrError or outputInvalid contribute nothing)

protocol.authorisation: owner, 2026-10-18: "I approve freezing the revised LRLPR-26 multi-frame aggregation protocol and authorise its bounded Development-only implementation and execution."
protocol.precedence: the protocol text is normative; this record is its machine form plus the pre-execution resolutions listed under 'resolutions'
protocol.status: FROZEN on owner approval 2026-10-18; this record, the protocol and the split file are committed together in the freezing commit, before any OCR call on LRLPR-26 data

resolutions.issue: The protocol's formula int(sha256('lrlpr26-split-v1|' + min_text), 16) % 2 does not reproduce its 'measured stratum counts' table; that table was produced by a pre-protocol probe that hashed the bare text (no prefix).
resolutions.resolution: The formula is normative and is applied as written (with the prefix). The split file records the resulting counts: A/Brazilian 2,440/2,560, A/Mercosur 2,533/2,467, B/Brazilian 1,038/962, B/Mercosur 4,077/3,923 (DEV/EVAL). Decided before any OCR call; outcome-blind.

resolutions.issue: Which images enter the byte-identical image grouping.
resolutions.resolution: All ten images (LR and HR) of every track, by the per-file manifest SHA-256. On this data the image unions merge no group beyond the text groups (16,946 groups = distinct texts).

resolutions.issue: The protocol does not state how 500-ID blocks are assigned or which conflict tracks are excluded.
resolutions.resolution: block = (scenario, trackNumber // 500); EVAL iff int(sha256('lrlpr26-block-v1|' + scenario + '|' + block), 16) % 2 == 1; a plate-identity group with tracks in both DEV and EVAL blocks is a conflict group and its EVAL-side tracks are excluded (the protocol's 'loses ... EVAL tracks'). Result, recorded in the split file: 943 conflict groups, 1,264 EVAL-side tracks excluded (all in Scenario A); the protocol's 1,484-1,738 came from the unprefixed probe.

resolutions.issue: Floating-point ties and threshold comparisons in A.
resolutions.resolution: w and the share are exact Fractions of the float64 confidences; tau is the exact decimal; ties are exact equality.

resolutions.issue: 'Median of three timed passes' when the protocol runs two OCR passes.
resolutions.resolution: A third full timing pass (phase 2T) is run under identical settings; its readings must also be canonical-equal (else INVALID).

resolutions.issue: Readings that pipeline.py would abstain for contract reasons.
resolutions.resolution: They are ineligible as 'outputInvalid' (see eligibility), reproducing summarise_track's admission.
The five directional measures: correctTextRecall, incorrectTextAcceptance, predictionPrecision, coverage, wrongTextsPerTrack (cost is identical for C and A).

resolutions.issue: The dataset record at e0cce486 gives train.zip SHA-256 fb95f86d8f5666ce..., but the held archive hashes to fb95f86dbf5666ce... (one hex digit, a transcription error; byte count 719,723,859 equal).
resolutions.resolution: Before freezing, all 220,000 file members of train.zip were compared with data.zip/train.tar (data.zip equals its Git LFS oid): identical paths and bytes. The record is corrected with a dated note in the freezing commit and the experiment binds the actual SHA-256.

secondary.blockSplit: phases 3-4 rerun on the split file's block assignment (500-ID blocks per scenario; conflict-group EVAL-side tracks EXCLUDED); thresholds re-selected on the block split's own DEV by the same selection rules; bootstrap CIs over plate-identity groups restricted to block-EVAL tracks, same seed and resamples
secondary.frameBudget: SB, U, C(k*) and A(tau*) (main-split selection, no re-selection) on the first 1, 3 and 5 LR frames of each EVAL track; OCR calls per track = frames used; C(k) with k greater than the frames used always abstains; A needs s >= 2 so it abstains at 1 frame
secondary.status: reported only; never feeds the decision

selection.choose: highest DEV correct-text recall among feasible configurations
selection.feasible: DEV incorrect-text acceptance <= 1.0% of DEV tracks, exactly: 100 * incorrectTracks <= devTracks
selection.infeasible: no feasible configuration: the family is INFEASIBLE at the target; its strictest configuration (k=5, tau=1.00) is scored on EVAL, labelled infeasible, reported descriptively and cannot be SUPPORTED
selection.output: selection.json (text-free); its SHA-256 is committed to the branch before phase 4
selection.population: DEV tracks of the main split only

comparisons: X - U for X in {C*, A*, S1, SB} and (secondary) U-raw - U, every measure
bootstrap.generator: numpy.random.default_rng(20261018); for each of 2,000 resamples in order, integers(0, G, size=G) over the EVAL groups sorted by group index; one shared sequence of resamples for every comparison (paired)
bootstrap.precisionUndefined: a resample where either precision is undefined is dropped for that statistic only, and the drop count is reported
bootstrap.statistic: difference of the two policies' measure on the pooled tracks of the resampled groups
bootstrap.unit: whole EVAL plate-identity groups (split-file group index)

mcnemar.status: exploratory only; tracks within a group are correlated, so p-values can overstate confidence
mcnemar.test: exact two-sided binomial test on discordant tracks: p = min(1, 2 * sum_{i<=min(b,c)} C(b+c, i) / 2^(b+c)); for the per-track correct indicator and the per-track incorrect indicator, X vs U and A* vs C*
